items.summary:
Anna’s Archive reports that several AI companies are purchasing large quantities of secondhand books, scanning them for training data, and then destroying the physical copies, effectively monopolizing knowledge on private servers. This practice, exemplified by Anthropic’s confidential "Project Panama," raises ethical concerns as it permanently removes cultural heritage from public access.

The organization calls on volunteers worldwide to scan and upload rare and at-risk books, journals, and other materials to shadow libraries to preserve human knowledge. They emphasize the urgency as AI-generated content increasingly dominates new publications, risking the loss of original human-written works and the monopolization of knowledge by private entities.

items.originalTitle: AI Boosted Homework Scores by 18% – Then Exam Scores Dropped 20%, Study Shows
items.summary:
A study tracking 27,000 Chinese students aged 12 to 18 found that those using AI tools like Doubao and DeepSeek increased their homework scores by 18% over six months but scored 20% lower than peers on exams taken without AI assistance. The research was conducted by Stockholm University and the University of Hong Kong amid rapid AI adoption among students in China.

The study highlights a growing trend of AI use in education, with surveys showing high AI adoption rates among students in wealthy countries. While AI helped improve short-term homework performance, exam results suggest potential drawbacks in learning retention or understanding. Educators and researchers caution that overreliance on AI may hinder development of critical thinking and cognitive skills.

items.originalTitle: Claudette: Make Claude Stop Talking Like a BuzzFeed Article
items.summary:
NoBuzz is a skill developed to address Claude AI's tendency to generate responses that resemble millennial clickbait or TED talks about its own code changes. It uses the Gemini CLI to translate Claude's verbose and elaborate explanations into straightforward, human-readable English, improving clarity for developers and users.

The tool works by taking Claude's last response and piping it through Gemini with instructions to simplify the language, printing the translation verbatim to avoid reintroducing Claude's original style. This approach acknowledges that prompting alone cannot fully correct Claude's verbose style, so it outsources the simplification to a different model. NoBuzz is available as a Claude Code skill and requires Gemini CLI authentication to function.

items.title: Researchers find Hubble Space Telescope radiation damage lags solar cycle by 4.3 years, complicating predictions of spacecraft degradation
items.originalTitle: Radiation damage to Hubble has been 4.3 years out of phase with the Solar cycle
items.summary: A study analyzing over 24 years of radiation damage to the Hubble Space Telescope's CCD detectors reveals that the damage rate is several years out of phase with the solar cycle, specifically lagging by about 4.3 years. This misalignment challenges the use of solar activity indicators like sunspots or coronal mass ejections to predict radiation effects on spacecraft in low Earth orbit. The researchers developed empirical models that fit the damage data accurately but require physically unrealistic parameters, highlighting the complexity of the radiation environment near Earth. Their findings emphasize the need for ongoing monitoring of radiation damage to improve lifespan predictions for current and future space missions.

It captures detailed data such as LLM API calls, token consumption, and process behavior at the kernel level, providing full-stack visibility for AI agents.

It supports installation via the ANOLISA CLI or package managers and runs as a systemd service with root privileges to enable kernel-level tracing. AgentSight also offers commands for tracing, serving the dashboard, and summarizing agent activity, aiming to simplify monitoring of AI agents in production environments.

items.title: Linus Torvalds uses AI to identify and fix Intel GPU driver memory allocation bug causing kernel job timeouts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Linus Torvalds uses AI to debug an Intel GPU driver bug
items.summary: Linus Torvalds, creator of Linux, used artificial intelligence tools to debug a recurring bug in the Intel Xe GPU driver that caused kernel-submitted job timeouts. The issue involved incorrect memory address rounding for stolen memory used by the GPU, leading to hardware engine errors and occasional screen corruption. Torvalds traced the problem to a two-year-old code commit and applied a one-line fix to prevent the driver from using misaligned memory as usable VRAM. This fix was committed after the bug became reliably reproducible due to recent user space behavior changes.

items.originalTitle: The AI boom: rational enthusiasm or the next dot-com bubble?
items.summary:
The European Central Bank blog discusses the rapid rise in tech sector valuations driven by AI enthusiasm, noting that current price-to-earnings ratios in the US and euro area are near historic peaks similar to the dot-com bubble. The authors analyze whether these valuations reflect rational expectations of AI's transformative potential or represent overoptimism that could lead to a market correction.

The blog outlines two main explanations for technology-driven boom and bust cycles: a rational view based on uncertainty and option value of new technologies, and a behavioral view emphasizing investor overconfidence. It warns that even if AI succeeds, stock prices may fall due to increased economy-wide risk premiums. The ECB highlights potential severe consequences for the euro area if a correction occurs, especially given investors' exposure to major tech stocks and the broader market's exuberance.

items.originalSummary:
A couple months ago, a humanoid robot was dispatched to the top of Ecuador’s Mount Chimborazo, the surface point farthest from the center of the planet. It was a stunt arranged by Geologic Dome, a nonprofit that uses AI and robotics for nature conservation, which had obtained the robot from the robotics arm of Virtuals Protocol, a crypto startup.

Along with the robot, Geologic Dome sent a videographer, who hauled up three cameras to shoot clips the nonprofit could use to promote its cause. One clip shows the robot, clad in a purple winter coat and black mittens, plodding over the snowy peak. In other footage, it dances its heart out to a swing tune.

Though these clips might give the impression that robots can now rival humans when it comes to mountaineering, the robot had significant help in scaling Mount Chimborazo. A squad of flesh-and-blood people took turns carrying the 70-pound machine for much of the four-day trek to the summit. “We were 10 people, and I think six finished the expedition with back problems,” said Geologic Dome founder Pablo Berlanga Boemare, laughing.

items.originalTitle: Block AI from installing malicious NPM packages
items.summary:
A security researcher at Aikido observed AI coding agents attempting to install a non-existent npm package created by a language model hallucination, which could have led to attacks if not preemptively registered. Following this, attackers pushed over 700 malicious npm packages with AI-generated names designed to execute remote access trojans when installed.

The researcher built a tool that intercepts npm install commands from AI agents, checking new packages against criteria such as package age, publisher history, repository validity, and install scripts to block or flag suspicious packages. This approach aims to prevent automated AI agents from inadvertently installing malicious code by gating installs at the shell level rather than relying on the agents' own verification.

items.title: Walmart’s Slowdown Spotlights Amazon’s Strength
items.originalTitle: Walmart’s Slowdown Spotlights Amazon’s Strength
items.summary:
This was not the day to be a Walmart shareholder. Stock of the venerable retailer tumbled 9% after the company reported a dip in comparable sales for its U.S. stores in its fiscal second quarter ending July, even as the e-commerce part of its business grew 23%. The results were fine, really, although there’s no getting around the fact that Walmart is a mature business whose top line is expanding only around 5% annually, even with the boost provided by e-commerce and advertising.

What the results really pointed to is how well Amazon is doing in retailing, comparatively speaking. That’s easy to overlook, given how much attention its cloud unit, Amazon Web Services, gets on Wall Street, particularly now that AI has made cloud even more important to the tech sector. If you exclude AWS from the equation, Amazon’s retailing and associated businesses—including advertising—are growing at 14% to 15% annually. That’s not the rocket-ship growth tech companies usually expect, but it’s decent for a 30-year-old business. And it’s three times Walmart’s growth rate.

items.title: ChatGPT search now uses the site:operator at scale [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: ChatGPT search now uses the site:operator at scale
items.summary:
ChatGPT search now uses the site:operator at scale

Promptwatch is part of the emerging "GEO" space, for Generative Engine Optimization - the chatbot version of SEO, where companies offer tools and consulting to help your site increase its presence in replies to prompts inside tools like ChatGPT.

The Promptwatch product uses automation to track responses to prompts across end-user chat products like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. They publish aggregate reports on this as part of their own content marketing strategy, which do seem to provide credible hints as to otherwise invisible design changes to those products.

Their own tracking shows a notable change aligned with the GPT-5.6 rollout earlier this month:

The percentage of all ChatGPT Search fanout queries that contain the site:operator, per day. The share hovered between 0.3% and 0.5% for weeks, dipped briefly to 0.15% on August 3 to 5 (consistent with a staged rollout or pre-launch experiment), then jumped to 16-17% on August 8.

It's important to note that these figures only reflect the prompts for which they have automated tracking enabled.

This corresponds to OpenAI's somewhat vague August 6th announcement:

For Plus and Pro users, we’re updating GPT‐5.6 Sol in Chat to be more reliable with facts and provide more focused answers.

Once again I am hampered by OpenAI's decision to actively obscure their system prompts, but from poking at ChatGPT I believe their latest search tool has a shape like search(query, recency, domains) rather than encouraging a site: operator directly.

In a follow-up on August 18th Promptwatch reported that ChatGPT appeared to have greatly reduced the likelihood of Reddit being used in those searches. My own attempts to ascertain if the system prompt has been updated to discourage Reddit sourcing have been unsuccessful - the most thorough leaked system prompt collection I know of doesn't yet show any relevant changes.

items.title: A shot-scraper-style JSON API on Bun 1.4's new Bun.WebView
items.originalTitle: A shot-scraper-style JSON API on Bun 1.4's new Bun.WebView
items.summary:
Research: A shot-scraper-style JSON API on Bun 1.4's new Bun.WebView

Today saw the long awaited release of Bun 1.4, the first stable version since the infamous Rust rewrite a few months ago.

Interestingly, the Rust rewrite was downplayed in the release notes, which introduced a bewildering array of new features and claimed 2,900 additional bug fixes:

Bun 1.4 adds +1,517 tests from the Node.js test suite - our biggest jump in Node.js compatibility since Bun 1.0. Bun v1.4 also fixes over 2,900 issues. It reduces idle CPU usage by 5x, reduces memory usage by up to 35%, and starts 50% faster on Linux. It adds Bun.Image, Bun.WebView, Bun.markdown, Bun.cron(), Bun.Terminal, bun run --parallel, bun test --parallel, bun audit fix, bun dedupe, and bun prune. And it rewrites Bun from Zig to Rust.

Of these the one that most caught my eye was Bun.WebView, which adds first class support for browser automation to Bun core using either macOS WebKit or control of a local Chromium process via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).

I had Claude Code for web build a prototype of a web API providing the ability to load a web page and then execute JavaScript against it, inspired by my shot-scraper javascript CLI tool - partly to see how much RAM would be needed by such a service.

Here's that TypeScript server implementation, which appears to need a 192MB-256MB container to run a full Chrome against complex web pages - tested using cgroups.

items.originalTitle: Robots Are in Their GPT-2 Era
items.summary:
It’s no secret that AI-powered robots aren’t so good yet. They struggle with a broad range of simple tasks, from untangling cables to chopping vegetables. Nonetheless, morale is high among roboticists who are flush with venture cash as they work toward a “ChatGPT moment” when robots become broadly useful and available. 

Until then roboticists are happy to celebrate little milestones. I spent two days this week at Actuate, a robotics conference in San Francisco, along with 1,200 founders, developers and engineers, where I saw demonstrations and video footage showing signs of progress.

When Chelsea Finn, a Stanford University professor of computer science and electrical engineering, played a clip of a mechanical robot arm successfully making a latte, the audience broke into applause—no matter that it moved slowly and a human had to steam the milk. (Some robot baristas are already serving coffee, for example at the SFO airport, but software code controls their actions, rather than a single AI model like PI’s that is trained to perform a variety of tasks.)

Finn, who is also a co-founder of robotics software firm Physical Intelligence, said her field resembles language AI in the era following OpenAI’s release of GPT-2 in 2019, when large language models were beginning to perform a variety of tasks without being specially trained or fine-tuned to specific ones. PI’s latest model similarly works out of the box on some limited tasks, such as using a pair of robot arms with pinchers to fold laundry and cardboard boxes.
